slides.title: The 4 biggest U.S. trade gaps
slides.sub: Ranked by the U.S. goods trade deficit with each country in September 2026.

slides.heading: #1 Mexico
body: In September, the U.S. imported $28.7 billion more in goods from Mexico than it exported there.
That was the biggest gap with any single country that month.

slides.heading: #2 Vietnam
body: The U.S. bought $25.3 billion more from Vietnam than it sold there in September.
That gap was bigger than the one with China ($17.9 billion).

slides.heading: #3 Taiwan
body: Imports from Taiwan jumped $4.2 billion in September to $27.3 billion.
The U.S. sold Taiwan $5.3 billion in goods that month.

slides.heading: #4 China
body: China ranked fourth in September, behind Mexico, Vietnam and Taiwan.
The total U.S. trade deficit that month was $105.0 billion.

slides.heading: Trade gap, Sept. 2026
slides.note: U.S. goods imports minus exports, by country

slides.takeaway: A trade deficit means buying more than you sell. Check your labels: where was your stuff made?

posts.caption:
A trade deficit with a country means the U.S. imports more goods from it than it exports there. In September 2026, the four biggest gaps were:

1. Mexico: $28.7 billion
2. Vietnam: $25.3 billion
3. Taiwan: $21.9 billion
4. China: $17.9 billion

Imports from Taiwan jumped $4.2 billion in September to $27.3 billion. Counting goods and services together, the overall U.S. trade deficit was $105.0 billion for the month.

Data: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and U.S. Census Bureau, September 2026 trade release (Nov. 4, 2026). Goods only for country figures.
